paper.title: Correcting DFT formation energies towards experimental accuracy using foundational MLIPs and latent-feature delta-learning
paper.research_summary: The paper presents a two-stage correction framework to improve the agreement of density functional theory (DFT) formation energies with experimental values. First, it leverages foundational machine learning interatomic potentials (fMLIPs), specifically PET-OMATPES trained at the r2SCAN level, to compute zero-shot formation energies on DFT-relaxed geometries, reducing mean absolute error (MAE) by over 40% relative to GGA without additional DFT calculations. Second, it trains classical machine learning models (KRR, RF, GPR) in a delta-learning framework using the latent features of the fMLIP to predict the residual between the fMLIP-estimated formation energy and experiment, achieving a final MAE below 50 meV/atom—comparable to experimental uncertainty—while controlling the impact on relative phase stability through careful regularization.

task.task_name_raw: Correcting DFT formation energies towards experimental accuracy
task.objective: Improve the agreement of DFT-calculated formation energies with experimental formation enthalpies
constraints: must be applicable to existing GGA databases without re-running DFT
must limit distortion of relative phase stability
output_goal: formation energies with MAE < 50 meV/atom vs. experiment
stability classifications (e.g., energy above hull) preserved or physically justified

evidence.text: Correcting DFT formation energies towards experimental accuracy using foundational MLIPs and latent-feature delta-learning

Our results validate and extend the established practice of combining PBEsol geometries with meta-GGA energies to the era of foundational MLIPs. Finally, we train classical machine learning models to further correct the formation energies in a delta-learning framework, where we use the information-rich latent features of the foundational MLIP.
These models further reduce the mean absolute error below 50 meV/atom, bringing it down to values comparable with the experimental uncertainty itself.

stages.stage_name_raw: Compare DFT formation energies against experimental formation enthalpies
stages.stage_goal: Quantify the initial discrepancy between DFT formation energies and experiment to establish baseline error metrics
stage_output: systematic bias identification (e.g., overbinding of oxygen)

evidence.text: We then compare the DFT calculated formation energies against experimental formation enthalpies (see Methods for dataset details).

Fig. 2 (top left) shows the systematic overestimation by GGA formation energies with respect to experimental values, especially for strongly bound systems [30]. The error metrics in Fig. 2 (bottom left) confirm the large MAE (>170 meV/atom) and a significant positive bias (ME ≈130 meV/atom); PBE and PBEsol perform similarly poorly on this subset.

stages.stage_name_raw: Evaluate zero-shot fMLIP formation energies on DFT geometries
stages.stage_goal: Assess improvement in formation energy accuracy using foundational MLIPs (PET-OMATPES) without structural relaxation

evidence.text: Fig. 2b shows that zero-shot formation energies [62] from the PET-OMATPES model [63, 64]—one of the top-performing models in community benchmarks at the time of publication [65], trained on the OMAT [66] and MATPES [37] datasets at the r2SCAN level—reduce the MAE by more than 40% when evaluated at the DFT (GGA) relaxed geometry.

stages.stage_name_raw: Train classical ML models in delta-learning framework using fMLIP latent features
stages.stage_goal: Learn empirical corrections to the zero-shot fMLIP formation energies using their latent features as input
stage_input: delta target (δ∆HMLIP_f = PET-OMATPES r2SCAN formation energy − experimental formation enthalpy)

evidence.text: Finally, we train classical machine learning models to further correct the formation energies in a delta-learning framework, where we use the information-rich latent features of the foundational MLIP.

We train classical ML models (KRR, Random Forest, and GPR) in a delta-learning framework to predict the residual between calculated or estimated formation energies and experiment. Using the latent features of PET-OMATPES as input, our best models achieve a MAE below 50 meV/atom...

stages.stage_name_raw: Evaluate ML-corrected formation energies against experiment
stages.stage_goal: Quantify final accuracy (MAE < 50 meV/atom) and assess impact on relative phase stability (stability flip rate)

evidence.text: These models further reduce the mean absolute error below 50 meV/atom, bringing it down to values comparable with the experimental uncertainty itself.

Fig. 3a shows the test MAE for each model and feature combination across 30 train-test splits... GPR and KRR achieve the best results: a MAE of 52 meV/atom for δ∆HPBEsol_f and 50 and 49 meV/atom for GPR and KRR on δ∆HMLIP_f, respectively.

stages.stage_name_raw: Select optimal model via regularization tuning
stages.stage_goal: Balance formation energy accuracy and stability reliability by selecting regularization strength (α) for KRR-LAP-LF
stage_input: MAE and stability flip rate metrics

evidence.text: Based on the trade-off in Fig. 4a and b, we select the KRR-LAP-LF model with α = 0.1.
